newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 26.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 26. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto, attending Monday's APEC summit in the Philippines, said industrialised nations should give developing nations a chance to progress as it would benefit the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, which comprises 18 economies on the Pacific Rim.
The government last month paid off $540.46 million of its high-interest debt to multilateral agencies ahead of schedule, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said.

Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo said his interview with German magazine Der Spiegel in which he reportedly said Indonesia treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs" had been manipulated. Belo denied making the remark and called for better relations between East Timor and the Indonesian government and military.
Newly-listed Bank BNI made a spectacular debut on the Jakarta Stock exchange yesterday, closing at 1,250 rupiah a share compared with an offer price of 850 rupiah.
